NO H8 ON QUINTUS. I <3 sorta quintus
NOT TO BE TAKEN LITERALLY

some think ima bit crazyhere but is it just me, or is every map realse or map in avicus like the same? here is what i mean


Im not gonna name maps here but i been looking on the recent map submissions and i realized that all the maps look very similar. Some look similar to Qunitus, and other maps i do not know.

Idk if its me but i see that in general, SOME avicus maps and new map releases have the same old gameplay, ahenistetics, block palatte, etc... There has the be a variety in maps,not just the same plain old map. ITs like you take Quintus and "ohh, ima modify it a bit, and bam"

Now im saying its bad but i hafta say its a bit bland and old so im suggesting that maps should be made with

Exciting game play
Cool Block platte patterns
and make unique maps that stand out.

Dnt use the same old blocks to make maps. Use other blocks as well and make the map different. Avicus needs a whole variety of different kinds of maps.

Anyways, this is just my opinion and idk if its just me or not. So feel free to discuss and please take note that im not hating on avicus maps.

replies.author: San_David
replies.body:
I think he means blocks like Stone Brick, Wool, Stained Clay, Glowstone, etc. You see those blocks combined with at least one other outlier a lot. What the OP is trying to say, in terms of block palette, is that these blocks are overused. Of course, you can't get away without a bit of color, hence the Wool and Stained Clay.

So, to answer your final question, here's a list of blocks that can be used without looking stupid, aren't overused (which, basically, only amounts to any block that doesn't have a gray color), and may or may not make for a good combo.

Wooden Planks
Nether Brick
Sandstone
End Stone
Colored Glass

And some other blocks, once 1.8 is supported...

Prismarine
Sea Lantern
Diorite
Red Sandstone

Of course, some of those combos won't work, like End Stone and Prismarine, but you get the point (hopefully). Most people should be able to make a good build using Jungle Wood and Nether Brick, or Prismarine and Diorite (and, speaking of the latter, I actually am making a map with Prismarine, Diorite, and Nether Brick.)

And, finally, if you want to prove me wrong on any of these, show me four maps that have any one of these, without using Stone Brick.

replies.author: Y0urm0m1
replies.body:
by same old blocks i mean by stone bricks, wools, glowstone etc.. I mean, they can be used sure in a map. The only problem is like how it is used. For example some maps use lanes that use the same block pattern like wool, glowstone, cobble stone, stone bricks as shown in rendevous, and the recent map releases (please look there for future reference) Notice how they have the same block patterns and the shape and style of the map is very similar to other maps. I suggest changing it up a bit like using maps that are more "nature style" (cant pinpoint the word) like Sandstorm and Venemous. I mean, its ok to use maps that have void gaps and i enjoy them and all. Maybe try using other blocks like quartz clay, stained glass, panes, etc.. There are a lot of blocks in minecraft and it is good if a map maker can utilize it creatively. Like any one can use stone bricks, glowstone and wool but how they use it is what makes a map stand out (as well as how it plays)

Now i didn't say the maps that are similar are bad. Some actually play out well but it kinda catches my eye that some are similar so im just suggesting that next time, add some variety to the kind of maps we make. TO be sure, i am not hating any maps.

@snowsx3

This is not coming from an expert map maker but in my opinion, what makes a map stand out is how the map maker uses the blocks the make something creative. A map should try to be unique or different from the others. Of coruse there will be similar themed maps but its up to the map maker on wheather or not he/she can use blocks nicely. A map that stands out should give you that feeling like "whoa, awesome map". It should also have somewhat unique gameplay style as well as the shape of a map. Take CherryLandMC. It uses clay blocks well, the map is flashy and it makes me go "Wow". Its gameplay also offfers tnt which makes it somewhat exciting. Terrain and aehensetics go along with it to. IF there is a flat lane in a map, it can add structures, or blocks like gravel piles and 2 block tall leaves with glowstone (just examples). The terrain should also be smooth and not be bland and flat. 

Cool patterns, what i mean is like in some maps, they use stones, glow stone, and sometimes wool. I have seen maps that commonly used these pattens. Maybe something different like quartz and nether, using different types ,of wood. I take the lobby as a good example of map, even though it isn't considered a map. The lobby looks unique because i noticed how the walls were aranged and it looked really cool. The shape and blocks they used for the lobby made it flashy and fancy. What i really mean is, try to use diffrent patterns of blocks when making a map like wood, clay, quartz, different stairs, wools, leaves etc..

As for exciting gameplay,i have worded a bit wrong. But it is nice for a map to have exciting gameplay. By gameplay wise, the common nebula maps i see is 2 monument islands on the left on right of spawn and thats it. Im not an expert on gameplay in maps but i think the monuments can be changed up a bit. Like there could be a map where there is 2 monuments and 1 monument can be in the front while the other could be in the back. Als, the monuments dont have to be obsidian all the time. There could be stone spheres as monuments and the team has to destroy that. To conclude, the map gameplay style?(not sure if i worded it right) should not be always 2 monument islands on the left and right of spawn. It should be different. Different gameplay is the word.



To conclude, i do not hate avicus maps. Similar maps with similar gameplay are ok. I dont hate them and some i really like. However, it is up to the map maker on how he makes the maps. Yes there will be similar maps that uses same blocks, shape, etc. There are maps that will always be the same themed. That is fine because its pretty hard not having the same theme but maps shouldn't use the same blocks, lane and shape of the map. You can have a snow themmed map with dark grass, dark logs, snow, ice, and water and it can just be an ice puddle but a great map would make it greative witha mixture of all so that the terrain can be mixed with greass, and ice, and snow. The pond could also have some ice and some water which makes the pond blend in and there could be logs as acceroies for the map. Try to make it different you know. I cant really pinpoint what i am trying to say so i hope you guys get it. This is not coming from an expert map maker map tester, etc.. This is  just based on my experience though so dont feel like im saying your maps are bad.  all i wanted to say is

Do your best to make maps and i encourage others to make maps that are geat and fancy so Avicus can be more fun and awesome. 

So im sorry it took so long and title should be changed to a certain majority. Ill make sure when i do these kinds of topics, i will elaborate so i apologize and i hope you can forgive me. chao and b back tommorw maybe.

I dont know a lot of maps in the rots and i am currently researching through them!

Stained clay/Quartz, the spruce wood with leaves and water and stuff. That's looks. Avicus kinda fell once when there were too many looks involved. 

You do have some interesting points, there are a lot of void maps (Maps focused on void/bridging) and lots of monuments are placed in pairs.
